Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-06
Requested Service/CPT: Bunion surgery (hallux valgus), CPT 28296
Treating Surgeon: Marchetti, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Appeals and Grievance Department:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 28296 (correction of hallux valgus with bunionectomy), issued on 2026-08-06, on the stated basis that "the requested procedure does not meet the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria." I request that Molina reconsider this determination under Molina Clinical Policy MCP-700, "Molina Clinical Policy – Foot Surgery: Bunionectomy" (Last Approval: 02/11/2026), which I understand to be the policy Molina applies to determine medical necessity for this procedure.

I have not been provided the specific internal review worksheet Molina's reviewer used, so to the extent my understanding of the applicable criteria differs from what was actually applied in my case, I ask that Molina identify the exact policy version and criteria relied upon in the denial and reconcile that with the analysis below.

Below I address, criterion by criterion, why the documented record supports medical necessity under MCP-700's coverage policy, which states that surgical correction "may be considered medically necessary when ALL the following criteria are met with accompanying documentation":

1. Skeletal maturity ("Member is > 18 years old, or has documented evidence of skeletal maturity")
[Patient's date of birth or other documentation of skeletal maturity is not included in the clinical summary provided to me and should be confirmed in the medical record already on file with Molina.]

2. Signs/symptoms directly attributable to hallux valgus
The policy requires "At least ONE of the following signs/symptoms directly attributable to a hallux valgus (HV) or bunionette deformity: a. Significant and persistent pain at first metatarsophalangeal (MTP) joint or fifth MTP joint b. Ulceration or skin breakdown at first MTP joint or fifth MTP joint c. Clinically significant functional limitation resulting in impaired ambulation." The record documents 18 months of progressive pain in the foot that is unrelieved by rest, together with an inability to tolerate closed shoes and documented ulceration risk over the bony prominence. This satisfies at least the "significant and persistent pain" prong, and the functional limitation regarding footwear tolerance further supports this criterion.

3. Six months of provider-directed conservative treatment
The policy requires "Clinically significant symptoms resulting in persistent pain and functional limitation despite at least 6 months of provider directed conservative treatment (e.g., alternative or modified footwear, protective cushions or taping, foot orthotics, pharmacotherapy, and/or debridement or trimming of hyperkeratotic lesions)." The record reflects NSAID therapy for 8 months with inadequate relief, an 8-week (24-visit) course of physical therapy/activity modification with a custom orthotic and wide toe-box footwear (2026-05-04 to 2026-06-29), and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-20 that provided only 4 weeks of partial relief. Taken together, this conservative treatment course spans more than 6 months and has failed to relieve the patient's symptoms, satisfying this criterion.

4. Adequate lower extremity vascular perfusion
The policy requires "Documentation of adequate lower extremity vascular perfusion (e.g., strong, palpable pedal pulses)." [The clinical summary provided to me does not include a specific vascular/pedal pulse examination finding. I ask that Molina review the pedal pulse or vascular findings already documented in Dr. Marchetti's exam note, or, if not yet documented, we will supplement the record with this finding.]

5. Radiographic confirmation of deformity severity
The policy specifies that for "Bunionectomy with Corrective Osteotomy," the radiographs must show: "i. 20 degrees or greater HVA, indicating moderate to severe HV deformity ii. 14 degrees or greater intermetatarsal angle (IMA), indicating moderate to severe deformity iii. No degenerative changes, absent or mild arthritis, at the MTP joint." Weight-bearing foot radiographs obtained 2026-07-01 show a hallux valgus angle of 38 degrees and an intermetatarsal angle of 17 degrees — both well above the 20-degree HVA and 14-degree IMA thresholds in the policy. [The radiology report's specific finding regarding degenerative changes/arthritis grading at the first MTP joint is not included in the clinical summary provided to me; I ask Molina to review the full radiology report already submitted with the prior authorization request, which I understand to document no more than mild arthritic change, and will supplement this appeal with that report if needed.]

Summary
Based on the above, the documented clinical record — 18 months of progressive, unrelieved pain; a conservative treatment course exceeding 6 months combining NSAIDs, physical therapy with orthotics and footwear modification, and corticosteroid injection, all with inadequate or only partial relief; weight-bearing radiographs showing an HVA of 38 degrees and IMA of 17 degrees; and documented functional limitation and ulceration risk — meets or exceeds the thresholds set out in MCP-700 for medically necessary bunionectomy with corrective osteotomy. I am not able to confirm from the summary in my possession whether the vascular perfusion and MTP-joint arthritis-grading elements of the criteria were separately documented; I ask that Molina review these elements in the full medical record already submitted, and I will promptly supplement the file with any additional documentation Molina identifies as missing.

I am not quoting or attributing any policy language above beyond the text retrieved directly from MCP-700 as identified. If Molina's reviewer relied on different or additional criteria, or a different version of the policy, I request that this be disclosed to me so that I may respond to it directly.

Please treat this letter as my written request for internal appeal of the adverse benefit determination referenced above. I request a copy of the complete medical policy, review criteria, and any medical/vocational expert reports relied upon in the original denial, per my rights under the plan and applicable law.

Enclosed/attached in support of this appeal:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-05-04 to 2026-06-29, 24 visits)
- Medication/injection records (NSAID trial, corticosteroid injection 2026-04-20)
- Weight-bearing foot radiographs and radiology report, 2026-07-01
- Office/exam notes from Dr. Marchetti documenting provocative testing, range of motion, and functional limitations
- [Any additional records confirming vascular exam findings and MTP joint arthritis grading, if available]

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and provide written notice of the outcome within the timeframe required under the plan and applicable Ohio and federal law. If this internal appeal is denied, I intend to pursue external review.

Sincerely,
